To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the synergistic effect between 365 nm irradiations and ionizing radiation in log‐phase cells is due to the induction of DNA lesions that are lethal under aerobic conditions and are repaired in anaerobic conditions.
the rec A gene‐mediated synergism between 364 nm and ionizing radiation is oxygen dependent, and is reversible by incubation in full growth medium.
365 nm radiation in the presence of oxygen causes a disruption of DNA repair in E. coli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of near‐UV radiation and ionising radiation on DNA in E. coli and the repair of such damage.
a model for near UV radiation inactivation of DNA repair deficient bacteria in which the oxygen dependence of inactivation is related to the disruption of DNA repair.
the effects of ionizing and non-ionizing radiation on biological systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synergism between 360 nm and ionizing radiation in logarithmic phase cultures of E. coli is due to a disruption of DNA repair, which is mediated through the rec A gene.
the oxygen‐dependent synergism is a result of a disruption of DNA repair and that the repair disruption is a result of damage to the photoreactivating enzymes.
the synergistic effect of 365 nm radiation and ionizing radiation is dependent on the rec A gene and that it is due to the disruption of the DNA repair mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
365 nm radiation inactivates cells in logarithmic phase cultures of E. coli K12 by a mechanism which is oxygen dependent, rec A dependent and rec B dependent.
the synergistic inactivation of colony forming ability of logarithmic phase E. coli by 365 nm and X‐rays is due to the induction of a repair‐disrupting lesion.
oxygen is a prerequisite for the lethal effect of 365 nm radiation on logarithmic phase E. coli cells.

the synergism between near UV and ionising radiation depends on the presence of the rec A gene.
